doc.title: Ken Peplowski interviewed by Monk Rowe, Aspen, Colorado, October 10, 1997 [interview 1 of 2]

title: Playing against a weak rhythm section
summary: Overcompensating with a poor rhythm section versus playing for yourself.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: What to think while improvising: wrong notes and being in the moment

blocks.x: Did you ever have the experience where you felt you had to play much, much harder because the rhythm section wasn’t good?

Oh yeah. And sometimes it’s the wrong thing to do. But you do it because you’re panicking and you’re trying to overcompensate. Sometimes it’s best to try and let yourself relax and just say, as I pointed out before, I’m going to ignore these people and just play for myself. Like if I was playing in a room or if I was rehearsing for Benny Goodman, I’m my own rhythm section, played the changes my own way, and then it really works well. And then you can kind of lift them up sometimes. Occasionally. Not always.
